gloss: degree of attention; level of interest; prominence
notes:
A compound noun frequently used in media, entertainment, and marketing to quantify or describe how much attention something is receiving. Often appears with {高|たか}い (high) or {低|ひく}い (low).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {注目度|ちゅうもくど}が{高|たか}い: to attract much attention
- {注目度|ちゅうもくど}が{低|ひく}い: to receive little attention
- {注目度|ちゅうもくど}が{上|あ}がる: attention increases
- {注目度|ちゅうもくど}ランキング: attention/popularity ranking
- {注目度|ちゅうもくど}ナンバーワン: number one in attention

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {人気|にんき}: popularity — focuses on being liked, not just noticed
- {話題性|わだいせい}: topicality, buzz — the quality of being talked about
- {知名度|ちめいど}: name recognition — how widely known something or someone is

ETYMOLOGY:
Composed of {注目|ちゅうもく} (attention, notice) + {度|ど} (degree, level).

definitions.gloss: degree of attention; level of interest; prominence
definitions.explanation: the extent to which something attracts public attention or interest; how noteworthy or prominent something is

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{注目度|ちゅうもくど}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: This movie is getting a lot of attention.

examples.japanese: SNSでの{注目度|ちゅうもくど}が{急上昇|きゅうじょうしょう}した。
examples.english: The level of attention on social media surged.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{選挙|せんきょ}は{過去|かこ}に{比|くら}べて{注目度|ちゅうもくど}が{高|たか}く、{投票率|とうひょうりつ}も{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: This year's election attracted more attention than in the past, and voter turnout also increased.
